company.name: Albion Patient Transport Services Ltd
company.description: Independent non-emergency patient transport (NEPTS) provider operating across Greater Manchester, Cheshire and parts of West Yorkshire under sub-contract to an NHS integrated care board (ICB) framework and to a private broker. Carries eligible patients to and from outpatient appointments, renal dialysis, day-case admissions, discharges and inter-hospital transfers. CQC registered for the transport regulated activity, PSV operator (O) licence holder, with mobility-matched ambulant, wheelchair-accessible and stretcher-capable vehicles plus trained ambulance care assistants (ACAs).

metadata.generatedNote: Example dataset reflecting a typical operating week (2026-06-22 to 2026-06-28) for a small UK non-emergency patient transport (NEPTS) provider. Reflects DVSA MOT, PSV operator (O) licence, EU/GB tachograph and drivers' hours, DVLA category B/D1 licensing, CQC registration, NHS eligibility and mobility assessment, appointment time-windows and standing dialysis orders, payer/broker billing with verified-visit (electronic proof of attendance), patient transport authorisation expiry, safeguarding and protected (confidential) patient records under UK GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018, BLS and moving-and-handling certification, and Companies House registration.

notes.author: Raymond Whitworth (DRV-01)
notes.body: Standing dialysis order ran to plan this morning. Used the key-safe to gain access, transferred the patient from his mobility scooter to the wheelchair and ramped him out without difficulty. Renal unit signed him off as fit to travel at 12:18 after a short wait for bloods. Key-safe re-secured on return. Treating this as a confidential patient record.

notes.author: Workshop (Manchester)
notes.body: W04 tail-lift platform will not lower under load; traced to a sticking control valve. Part on order from the lift distributor. LOLER thorough examination of the lift is due at the same time so we will complete both before the MOT on 29 June. Vehicle remains VOR; ambulant work moved to spare A03.

notes.author: Tariq Mahmood (DRV-03)
notes.body: Stretcher discharge from the Countess of Chester completed safely. Patient on 2 L/min oxygen throughout; cylinder pressure was getting low by the end of the run so flagged for a reserve swap at the depot. Used the carry-chair through the front doorway and handed over to the patient's own concentrator at home. Discharge letter and TTOs handed to family.

notes.author: Denise Holloway (DRV-05)
notes.body: Broker booking for MedTransport. Per-mile plus waiting tariff so I started the mileage and waiting clock at the consultation and the patient signed the timesheet at the end confirming 52 minutes waiting. Verified-visit captured at both ends. Paperwork goes back to Neil at the broker for the insurer claim.

notes.author: Operations
notes.body: Heads-up for the planners: the authorisation on this Salford booking (PTS-AUTH-45001) expires on 15 August. This journey is covered but anything after that date must be re-authorised by the ICB before we accept it. Flagged on the patient record so it does not slip through.

notes.author: Transport Manager
notes.body: Colin's Driver CPC card expires on 4 July and his BLS certificate at the end of July. He is on annual leave until 6 July, so the periodic CPC training and BLS refresher are both booked to complete before he returns to driving duties. He must not be rostered until both are renewed.

notes.author: Marta Kowalczyk (DRV-04)
notes.body: Bariatric transfer planned for tomorrow. Done the pre-journey risk assessment: 210 kg patient, hoist transfer at both ends, double crew with Tariq, reinforced vehicle B01. Confirmed the receiving site has bariatric equipment available. Single-use authorisation only covers the transfer leg.

notes.author: EV Supervisor
notes.body: Electric WAV averaged 0.31 kWh/km on the Wythenshawe run today including the tail-lift power draw. Mid-day opportunity charge at depot bay 2 took it from 41% back to 78% in under an hour, plenty for the afternoon. State of health steady at 98%.

notes.author: Account Manager
notes.body: Confirmed the Q3 standing dialysis orders with Sister Ashcroft at the MRI renal unit. AM slots Monday/Wednesday/Friday and PM slots Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday continue unchanged. Two patients up for transport-authorisation renewal at the end of September; we will prompt the ICB in good time so there is no gap in cover.

notes.author: Stephen Atherton (DRV-06)
notes.body: Powered-wheelchair patient from the first-floor flat collected using the stairclimber with the carer assisting. Four-point Unwin securement applied in the WAV and checked before moving off. Clinic confirmed fit to travel on return. No issues.

notes.author: Workshop
notes.body: Reserve oxygen cylinder fitted to S01 after the morning discharge run brought the working cylinder down to around 149 bar. Both cylinders are within their test dates. Medication fridge logging steady between 4 and 5 degrees throughout the shift.

notes.author: Karen Tomlinson (customer)
notes.body: Thank you to the crew again this week. Mum likes having the same drivers for her physio runs, it makes a real difference to her confidence. The pickup was bang on time and she was home well before lunch. Prepayment for next week is sorted.

notes.author: Tester (ATF Manchester)
notes.body: DVSA MOT passed for fleet A01 (Class 4) with no advisories. Brakes, lamps, tyres and structure all within limits. Certificate issued and uploaded to the vehicle file.

notes.author: Operations
notes.body: Updated the access notes for this patient's home on the protected record: key-safe code held securely in the system, ramp at the front door, scooter-to-wheelchair transfer in the hallway. Standing dialysis order so the same access applies three mornings a week. Record marked confidential - crews only see what they need for the journey.
